title: Can five so-so models beat one?
hook: Each model is right only 60% of the time. Does letting them vote help at all?

knows: that a model can be right a certain share of the time
that averages settle down over many tries
doesNotKnow: that a majority vote of weak models can beat each one
that the gain depends on the models making different mistakes

misconception: Combining 60%-accurate models still gives a 60%-accurate answer.
objective: The learner can explain that a majority of independent voters is wrong only when most are wrong at once, which is rarer than one being wrong, and that shared mistakes remove the gain.

claims.text: If five independent models are each right with chance 0.6, their majority vote is right with chance 0.683 (at least 3 of 5); with 21 voters, 0.826.
In the first seeded batch of 200 questions, one model got 121 right, a vote of five 138 and a vote of 21 158.
claims.source: voteRight(1, n, false) in Demo.tsx; batch b uses mulberry32(b), batches shown in order 1, 2, 3, ..., untuned. Spread: in 2,000 batches the vote of five beat the single model in 1,967.

claims.text: When every voter copies the same answer ('same mistakes'), the vote is right exactly when one model is: 60% in the long run.
claims.source: By construction: voteRight(b, n, true) gives every voter voter 1's outcome, so the majority equals voter 1. Batch 1: 121/200 for any n.

claims.text: The models are toys (coin flips with chance 0.6), labelled 'Toy models' on the stage; independence is an assumption stated in the question.
A vote helps only as far as the voters are wrong in different places.
claims.source: Shown in the toy (c1 vs c3). For real ensembles: Dietterich 2000, 'Ensemble methods in machine learning', Multiple Classifier Systems, LNCS 1857 (an ensemble beats its members when they are accurate and make different errors); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009 §8.7 (bagging; correlation between members limits the gain, §15.2).

recall.question: You combine three spam filters by majority vote. When does the vote help most?
options: When the filters tend to make mistakes on different emails
When the filters were trained the same way on the same data
It never helps: the vote is only as good as the average filter
recall.why: The vote is wrong only when most filters are wrong on the same email. If they err in different places that is rare; if they err together the vote is no better than one.
